chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu‘allā ibn Muhammad, from Al-Washshā’, from ‘Alī ibn Al-Hasan, from Safwān Al-Jammāl, who said:
I asked Abā ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام about the Master of this affair, so he said: “Indeed, the Master of this affair does not amuse himself and does not play.”
And Abū Al-Hasan Mūsā عليه السلام came forward while he was young, and with him was a Meccan she-goat kid, and he was saying to it: “Prostrate to your Lord.”
So Abū ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام took him and drew him close to himself, and said: “May my father and my mother be for the one who does not amuse himself and does not play.”

key_terms.بِأَبِي وَأُمِّي: an expression of deep reverence and endearment
key_terms.صَاحِبِ هَذَا الْأَمْرِ: the one vested with this divinely appointed authority, referring to the Imam
key_terms.عَنَاقٌ مَكِّيَّةٌ: a young she-goat described as Meccan
key_terms.لَا يَلْعَبُ: does not play in a frivolous manner
key_terms.لَا يَلْهُو: does not engage in idle amusement or distraction

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith indicate the Imamate of Imam Mūsā al-Kāẓim عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a sign of the Imam through seriousness and freedom from frivolity, even in childhood. It also depicts Abū ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام indicating the special station of Abū Al-Hasan Mūsā عليه السلام through word and gesture.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Washha, from Ali Bin Al Hassan, from Safwan Al Jammal who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the Master of this command (Imamate), so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The Master of this command would ‘لَا يَلْهُو وَ لَا يَلْعَبُ’ neither (indulge in) games nor play’,

and Abu Al-Hassan Musa<sup>asws</sup> came over, and he<sup>asws</sup> was young, and with him<sup>asws</sup> was a Meccan kid (baby goat), and he<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘Prostrate to your Lord<sup>azwj</sup>!’

So Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> grabbed him<sup>asws</sup> and embraced him<sup>asws</sup> to himself<sup>asws</sup> and said: ‘By my<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> and my<sup>asws</sup> mother! The one<sup>asws</sup> who neither (indulges in) games nor play’.
en.sarwar: 15. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla ibn Muhammad from al-Washsha’ from Ali ibn al-Hassan from Safwan al-Jammal who has said the following.
“I asked abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) about the in charge of this matter (Leadership with Divine Authority) nad he said. “ The in charge of the task does not trifle or play.
At this time abu al-Hassan, Musa came. He was very small. With him there was a baby goat of Makka and he was saying to her, “Prostrate before your Lord.
Abu ‘Abdallah then took him and hugged him and said, “May Allah take my soul and the souls of my parents in service for the cause of one who does not trifle and engage in amusement.”
